newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher on oversold signs, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher on oversold signs, soybeans.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on signals the market was oversold and a late surge in soy added to the advances, traders said.

The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for July closed Tuesday at 17 percent which, along with other technical indicators, indicated the market was oversold and due for a recovery. An RSI of 30 or less is considered an oversold market. July's RSI Wednesday closed at 31 percent.
Fundamentals were little changed as Midwest weather, while a bit cool for proper germination and growth of the crop, remained overall bearish for corn futures, the traders said.

The new crop December on Tuesday fell to a two-year low and at Wednesday's close had lost another two cents per bushel in its spread with the nearby July. The July/December spread closed Wednesday at 14-1/4 cents per bushel, premium July.
Traders said the July contract Wednesday was supported by slow farmer selling and firm cash basis markets.
USDA Tuesday said the U.S. corn crop as of Sunday was 95 percent seeded, well above the 76 percent pace of a year ago and above the 81 percent average pace.
Corn closed 1-3/4 to 5-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with July up 5-1/4 at $2.69-1/2.

Pit sources said the fund activity Wednesday was about evenly divided between long and short positioning but Rosenthal Collins the key buyer of four million bushels of December and three million July. Smith Barney bought four million bushels of July, traders said.
Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold five million bushels of July and LIT America sold three million bushels of July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 73,000 contracts, above the 69,495 traded Tuesday.

Spread traders said Continental Grain legged three million July/December, Term Commodities did three million July/December at 12 to 12-1/2 cents, premium July and Term also did three million July/September at 10-1/2 cents, premium July.

In corn options, Rand Financial sold 400 July $2.70 calls at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 cents, Smith Barney bought 400 July $2.80 calls at 2-1/4 cents and Cargill Investor Services bought 500 July $2.90 calls at 1-1/2 to 1-3/8 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, slightly above the 19,128 traded Tuesday.
